Action.description:
A command (`[source]`, `[transform]`, `[generator]`, `[verify]`).

Evidence runs commands; it has no built-in knowledge of any data source. Anything that can
be fetched or computed by a program (`curl`, `git`, `bq`, `jq`, an SBOM tool, an AI agent)
can be evidence. The program runs without a shell; placeholders such as `{output}` and
`{input.NAME}` are expanded in `run`, `env`, `cwd`, and `locator` (see `docs/format.md`).

cwd.description: Working directory, relative to the evidence file. Defaults to its directory.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the program.

interval.description:
`[source]` only: minimum time between refreshes by `evidence update` (e.g. `6h`,
`1d`). Without an interval the source is refreshed only explicitly.

locator.description:
Where the content came from, recorded in the state after each successful run: a fixed
value (placeholders expanded) or a command whose trimmed standard output is the value,
e.g. `commit = ["git", "-C", "{output}", "rev-parse", "HEAD"]`.

stdin.description:
File fed to the program's standard input (relative to the evidence file), e.g. a SQL
query or an AI prompt.

stdout.description: Write the program's standard output to `{output}` (instead of the program writing it).

timeout.description: Kill the program after this long (default: `execution.timeout` from the config).

Claim.description: A claim: a range of the subject and the evidence it is based on.

evidence.description: Evidence backing the range. Empty only when `origin = "primary"`.

origin.description: Declares the range as primary information.

select.description: The range of the subject this claim covers.

anchor.description:
The claimed text at review time, used to re-anchor the claim after edits
(only kept for short ranges).

content.description: Hash of the claimed range of the subject at review time.

reviewed_at.description: When the claim was last reviewed.

author.description: Who wrote an authored subject: `human`, `ai:<agent>`, a name, …

claims.description: `authored`: ranges of the subject and the evidence they are based on.

format.description: Subject format. Inferred from the subject's extension when omitted.

generator.description: `authored`: optional command (e.g. an AI agent) that regenerates the subject.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the project.

inputs.description: `derived` (and `authored` generators): other evidence this subject is computed from.

lifecycle.description: How the subject relates to upstream change. Defaults to `living`.

members.description:
Makes the subject a list (a JSON array or JSONL) whose entries are kept as member
pairs, each generated from a template and updated on its own.

origin.description: `authored`: declares the whole subject as primary information (no upstream evidence).

schema.description: Schema the subject must conform to.

source.description: `source`: the command that acquires the subject.

state.description: Tool-managed state. Never edit by hand.

subject.description:
Where the subject lives: a path relative to this evidence file's directory, or
absolute. Defaults to this file's own path without `.evid` (the sidecar layout). A
subject outside the project works, but draws a `subject-outside-project` warning.

tags.description: Free-form tags for search and grouping.

transform.description: `derived`: how the subject is computed from its inputs.

verify.description: Optional check run on every new version of the subject before it is accepted.

path.description: For directory subjects: path of the file inside the directory.

select.description: Part of the referenced subject; the claim only becomes stale when this part changes.

anyOf.description: Evidence id and a selector into its subject.

EvidenceRef.description: A reference from a claim to evidence, optionally to a part of it.

oneOf.description: JSON document.
JSON Lines (one JSON value per line); schemas apply to each line.
TOML document.
Markdown text.
Plain text.
A directory.
Opaque binary data.

as.description: Name used in placeholders (`{input.<name>}`); defaults to the id.

oneOf.description: Primary information acquired automatically by a command.
Deterministically computed from other evidence.
Written by a human or an AI.

Lifecycle.description: How a subject relates to upstream change.

oneOf.description:
One-off artifact pinned to the evidence it was written against; never becomes stale
because of upstream change.
Must track upstream; becomes stale when referenced evidence changes.

anyOf.description: A fixed value; placeholders except `{env.NAME}` are expanded.
A command (no shell) whose trimmed standard output is the value.

LocatorValue.description: A locator entry: a value or a command printing the value.

Member.description: A member of a list. Its definition is composed from the parent's `[members]` template and the list entry; any other evidence file field overrides the template for this member only.

member.description: Key of this member's entry in the parent's list.

member_of.description: Id of the parent evidence, whose subject is the list.

MemberState.description: The list entry a member was produced from.

fields.description:
Its top-level text, number, and boolean fields, so the member's definition can still be
composed after the entry left the list.

id.description: Id of each member, e.g. `space-{member.id}`. Use the key field so ids stay stable.

key.description:
JSON Pointer to the stable key of each list entry, e.g. `/id`. Members are matched to
entries by this key, so a member keeps its history when other fields change.

on_removed.description: What `evidence update` does with a member that is no longer listed. Default `keep`.

subject.description:
Subject of each member, relative to this evidence file's directory, e.g.
`pages/{member.path}.md`. The member's evidence file is the sidecar of its subject.

template.description:
Definition shared by every member: any evidence file field except `version`, `id`,
`subject`, `members`, and `state`. `kind` defaults to `source`. Strings may use
`{member.FIELD}` (a top-level text, number, or boolean field of the entry).

OnRemoved.description: What happens to a member that is no longer listed.

oneOf.description: Keep it and report `member-removed` until it is removed with `evidence remove`.
Delete it, unless other evidence depends on it (then keep it and report it).
Primary information: intentionally not backed by other evidence.

fragment.description: Hash of the selected fragment at pin time (when the reference has a selector or path).

snapshot.description: Snapshot of the referenced subject at pin time.

oneOf.description: A new snapshot was accepted.
The run succeeded and the content did not change.
The run, schema validation, or verification failed; the previous snapshot was kept.

json_schema.description: Path to a JSON Schema, relative to the evidence file.

Selector.description: Names a part of a document.

oneOf.description: The whole document.
A 1-based inclusive line range.
A Markdown section by heading text. Leading `#`s, if given, also constrain the level.
An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer.
Lines between a `span:NAME` marker line and a `/span:NAME` marker line.

SnapshotIdSchema.description: Content id: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex characters.

State.description: State written by the tool after runs and reviews. Humans must not edit it.

checked_at.description: When the subject was last successfully checked against its source (even if unchanged).

claims.description: Pins of each claim, recorded at review.

inputs.description: Snapshot of each input used by the last successful run.

last_run.description: Result of the most recent run.

locator.description: Where the content came from (the evaluated `locator` table, e.g. a git commit).

member.description: Members: the parent's list entry this member was last produced from.

snapshot.description: Snapshot of the subject accepted by the last successful run or review.

updated_at.description: When the subject content last changed.

description: Evidence file describing where a subject comes from. Usually a sidecar `<subject>.evid` next to the subject; `subject` places the subject elsewhere.
